correctness.rationale: Verified the exact statement for all fixed d≥2, positive side lengths and Haar sphere U. For q_i=∏_{j≠i}a_j>0, the orthotope facet formula gives B_Q(U)=Σq_i|U_i| and the positive bijection a_i=(∏q_j)^{1/(d−1)}/q_i. Gaussian polar independence G=RU yields h_k=E||G||^k m_k, with E||G||^k=2^{k/2}Γ((d+k)/2)/Γ(d/2). For half-normal X=|N(0,1)|, log M_X(z)=z²/2+log(1+tF(z)), t=√(2/π) transcendental and F(z)=z+O(z³)∈Q[[z]]; the k-th cumulant has nonzero degree-k coefficient (−1)^{k−1}(k−1)!t^k, proving κ_k≠0 for EVERY k without extrapolation. Cumulant additivity gives K_k=κ_k Σq_i^k; Newton identities recover all positive q roots from the first d moments. Constant-term perturbations of distinct-root polynomials yield continuous positive noncongruent q families with identical first d−1 moments. Smooth bounded moment-to-coefficient conversion plus the polynomial-root matching theorem/Rouché argument yield a uniform 1/d Hölder bound on side intervals [ℓ,L]; Vandermonde invertibility yields local Lipschitz at distinct facets; scaled pairs near q=(1,…,1) with equal lower symmetric functions and differing e_d by Θ(ε^d) force optimal exponent exactly 1/d. All normalization, repeated-root cases, and side-bound dependences are consistent. Independent symbolic checker confirmed 11 leading half-normal cumulant coefficients, the positive facet/side inverse for dimensions 2..8, a real cubic constant-term perturbation, and reconstructed the exact seven-entry Git source tree; these bounded checks are not proofs of universal statements.
residual_risks: The analytic proof uses established transcendence of π and classic complex-root matching; the finite symbolic checker does not establish all dimensions.
No finite-sample, nonorthogonal or orientation-recovery guarantee; constants may grow with d and with ℓ/L.

Beauzamy (1999) describes Ostrowski degree-d root-matching Hölder exponent 1/d, sharp in general, and Lipschitz stability of simple roots. This applies after the prior analytic moment-to-polynomial coefficient inversion.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The stronger width-moment theorem covers the central reconstruction/minimality and the exact nonstandard cumulant lemma; general polynomial coefficient-root stability covers the quantitative exponent upper bound. The submitted near-cube sharpness is elementary from Abas Proposition 3.6 under q=1+εu and a second constant-term perturbation family, yielding moment distance Θ(ε^d) and side distance Θ(ε). The exact compact constant is not provided in prior but follows by bounded smooth coefficient maps; it is not a newly independent structural result.

originality.rationale: A genuinely prior primary paper by Omri Abas (arXiv:2608.06348v1, submitted 2026-08-06) proves essentially the same all-dimensional finite moment reconstruction and generic sharp moment count, plus the SAME all-order nonvanishing of standard half-normal cumulants by the transcendence-of-pi highest-degree polynomial argument. By exact zonotope/Cauchy facet formula B_Q(U)=sum_i q_i|U_i|=W_q(U), with q_i=prod_{j!=i}a_j and a_i=(prod_j q_j)^(1/(d−1))/q_i, the submitted brightness distribution is the previously solved orthotope width distribution under a smooth bijective parameter change. Abas Theorem 3.5 proves first d moments recover q; Proposition 3.6 proves d−1 fail generically. The remaining compact-uniform 1/d Hölder continuity and simple-root Lipschitz property follow from classical polynomial-root perturbation estimates (Ostrowski, documented by Beauzamy 1999), and its near-cube optimality from the same scaled constant-term perturbation. Thus no independently novel final all-dimensional tomography theorem survives. This is demonstrated implication, not inference from shared titles or search absence.
residual_risks: Abas 2026 is a publicly available preprint, not claimed peer reviewed; its 2026-08-06 arXiv posting predates the 2026-10-11 assigned research package and directly covers the reconstruction, moment-count minimality, and half-normal nonvanishing argument.

The assigned compact-interval 1/d stability and near-cube sharpness are not stated verbatim in inspected Abas §3.4, but coefficient-to-root 1/d continuity and local simple-root Lipschitz bounds are classical (Ostrowski/Beauzamy). The near-cube sharpness follows by the same constant-term polynomial perturbation as Abas Proposition 3.6, scaled toward a multiple root; no independent new inverse invariant remains.

The original 1947 Walters full text and the 2026 three-dimensional companion full text were not independently read; stronger arXiv:2608.06348 full relevant proofs make this access limitation nondecisive.

Finite symbolic checks of 11 cumulant orders, dimensions 2..8 and one cubic root-perturbation family cannot prove an all-dimensional theorem; the PASS rests on reconstructing the analytical all-order transcendence argument, Gaussian factorization, Newton identities and Rouché/polynomial-root continuity.
Exact population moments only; no finite-sample statistics, arbitrary oblique parallelepipeds, or labeled-orientation recovery is assessed.

value.rationale: Reconstructing a positive d-parameter orthotope from d isotropic scalar moments and quantifying near-cube instability are natural inverse-geometry questions. However this precise first-d reconstruction, generic d−1 sharpness and the critical half-normal cumulant nonvanishing proof are all established in the earlier Abas 2026 all-dimensional width paper, whose random observable is EXACTLY the same after an invertible facet-area substitution. The residual 1/d continuity is a standard Ostrowski degree-d polynomial-root bound following mechanically from that published reconstruction, and local simple-root Lipschitz continuity is equally standard. The near-cube exponent witness is a routine scaled version of the published constant-term perturbation. There is no independently undetermined exact invariant, motivated structural lemma or new boundary theorem remaining to carry mathematical value as a research claim; correctness and reproducibility alone do not change this. The result remains a valid restatement/conditioning exercise useful for exposition.
residual_risks: A specialized statistical estimator with explicit optimal constants or noisy data bounds could be valuable, but no such theorem is claimed or proved in the submitted package.
The quantitative root estimate is a useful corollary yet does not independently overcome full earlier coverage of the stated inverse theorem.
